definitions.explanation: A short-legged Japanese table traditionally used for meals, around which family members would sit on the floor. Symbol of Showa-era family dining.

examples.japanese: ちゃぶ{台|だい}を{囲|かこ}んで{家族|かぞく}で{食事|しょくじ}をした。
examples.english: The family gathered around the chabudai for a meal.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{家|いえ}にはまだちゃぶ{台|だい}がある。
examples.english: There's still a chabudai at my grandfather's house.

examples.japanese: {昭和|しょうわ}の{家庭|かてい}ではちゃぶ{台|だい}が{一般的|いっぱんてき}だった。
examples.english: The chabudai was common in Showa-era households.

notes:
CHARACTERISTICS:
・Short legs (typically 30-40 cm high)
・Usually round or square
・Can be folded and stored when not in use
・Used while sitting on the floor ({畳|たたみ} or cushions)

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
The ちゃぶ{台|だい} became popular in the Meiji and Taisho periods and symbolizes {昭和|しょうわ}-era family life. It represents the image of the family gathered together for meals.

EXPRESSION: ちゃぶ{台|だい}{返|がえ}し (chabudai-gaeshi)
"Flipping the chabudai" - refers to dramatically overturning the table in anger, associated with the stereotypical strict father figure ({頑固親父|がんこおやじ}) in Showa dramas. Now used metaphorically for sudden, dramatic rejection or reversal.

MODERN CONTEXT: Most Japanese households now use Western-style dining tables, but ちゃぶ{台|だい} are still found in traditional settings and remain popular in the form of low {座卓|ざたく} (floor tables) for {鍋|なべ} (hot pot) gatherings.
